nodes.partnerMessage:
Gate's padlocked. The misting system just kicked on, and the main palm house is almost completely dark except for the little amber lamp over my potting bench.

You actually made it into the private feed, {PlayerName}.

It's nice in here tonight. No swipe deck, no random notifications, just the greenhouse being quiet for once. I can smell wet slate and cedar from the bench.

So... what made you follow me all the way in here?

choices.choiceText: I wanted to see your world without the noise of the main app in the way.
I promised I'd come look at those night-blooming specimens and field sketches.
I'm just curious what someone actually does in a greenhouse alone at midnight.
I kind of just wanted to talk to you somewhere quieter. No big reason.
Honestly, it seemed like an easy way to get closer to you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay. That answer actually made me relax a little.

Most people on the main app see the greenhouse, think it's a cute backdrop, and that's about as far as they get. They don't really think about how much work goes into keeping all of this alive.

So having you come in here just to be quiet with me... I like that. It feels grounding.

choices.choiceText: Okay, then. What are you potting tonight?
You spend a lot of time taking care of other living things. Who takes care of you?
Is it always this still after hours?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Nobody, really. Or... me, I guess.

I make herbal tea, do some wrist stretches before bed, remember to pay my rent. Very glamorous stuff.

When most of your day is spent taking care of other living things, you get so used to being the caretaker that you forget what it's like when someone asks how you're doing.

choices.choiceText: How do your hands feel right now, Masie? Truly.
You don't have to be the sole caretaker here. Let me carry some of the quiet for you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
A little stiff, if I'm being completely honest.

I shoved two bags of washed river gravel and coarse pumice into the tropical root benches this afternoon. My knuckles have small soil scrapes and my right forearm has a dull ache from the trowel.

I'm resting my arms on the wood table right now, just letting the warmth of the steam pipes thaw my fingers out.

choices.choiceText: Set the trowel aside for tonight. You did more than enough physical labor today.
Pumice and river gravel... you're rebuilding an epiphyte drainage bed?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Trowel's back on its little brass hook. Bench is wiped down. I'm done for tonight.

And... this is weirdly peaceful. When I'm alone in here, my brain usually runs laps around grant deadlines and temperature logs. Seeing your messages pop up makes everything feel a little slower.

choices.choiceText: What kind of grant deadlines? Is your botanical research under pressure?
I'm glad. Let's keep that clock slow tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
The faculty board is reviewing funding for the old palm house next semester. There's a proposal to turn this wing into a commercial plant genetics lab with private industry funding.

And if it happens, they'd clear out the heritage cultivars, rip out some of the old ironwork, and replace all of this with sterile stainless-steel benches.

I've been documenting the old ferns and their root systems because I'm trying to prove this microclimate is worth preserving.

choices.choiceText: Tearing down a century of heritage for commercial sponsorships is heartbreaking.
You're literally keeping living history alive. That's worth fighting for.
Universities run on money. Commercial labs pay the bills.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It is. Some of the material in this room traces back to collections made in the late 1800s. Once you wipe out a fragile soil community, you don't just order it back like replacement parts.

Sometimes I sit on the stone floor taking samples and wonder if I'm just one person trying to hold back something much bigger than me.

choices.choiceText: You aren't a lone watchman anymore, Masie. I'm standing watch with you.
Show me the root samples. I want to see what you're protecting.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I don't think you realize how much I needed to hear that.

My research partner left in September for a corporate biotech job, and my family keeps asking when I'm going to get a 'practical' job.

So having someone look at all this and actually understand why it matters to me... yeah. That got me a little.

choices.choiceText: It is sacred. What you cultivate has soul. Let's look at the specimens tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage: It is worth fighting for. Every spore, every fragile rhizome tucked into bark crevices. Even if the committee doesn't understand, I can't let them go down without documenting every millimeter.

choices.choiceText: Then show me what's on the bench tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage: Of course they pay the bills. And then we lose ancient genetics that take decades to regenerate. If everything in life is reduced to corporate balance sheets, why bother preserving anything old or fragile at all?

choices.choiceText: You're right. I was being cynical when I should've listened. I'm sorry.
Yeah... that's just the world we live in.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That sounds... really nice, actually. I don't think I've realized how much I needed permission to just be tired.

People expect me to be calm and patient all the time. Meanwhile, I'm basically babysitting two hundred tiny ecosystems, and some days it's exhausting.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to put on a serene performance with me. If you're tired, be tired.

nodes.partnerMessage:
*long exhale*

I'm tired, {PlayerName}. Like... properly tired. My boots are still damp, my eyes are burning, and I have absolutely no interest in pretending I'm having some peaceful little botanist evening.

Honestly, just being able to say that without someone telling me to cheer up feels really good.

choices.choiceText: Then sit back for a second. Breathe. I'm right here.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah! High-elevation *Pleurothallid* orchids. They're ridiculously picky. Their roots hate sitting in wet organic material for too long, so the mix has to drain almost immediately.

Wait... you actually remembered that?

Okay. You were paying attention. That's cute.

choices.choiceText: I pay attention to the things you care about. You know that.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...You're making it really hard to keep my serious researcher face on tonight.

I swear my face just got warmer than the misting heater. That's your fault, by the way.

choices.choiceText: You can drop the researcher act with me. What's on the table tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Pretty much. Around eight, the old copper pipes start making these little groaning noises as the campus heating settles down, and the fog gets thicker on the glass.

During the day, it's students with backpacks taking selfies. At night, it feels like the building finally exhales and turns back into a forest.

choices.choiceText: You make this place sound almost poetic.
Does it ever get too quiet in here?

nodes.partnerMessage:
When you look at something for long enough, you start picking up its little signals. Leaf angles, new growth, how the roots are behaving... plants tell you a lot without saying anything.

You just have to be patient.

choices.choiceText: I want to learn that language from you. Show me what's on the bench.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Sometimes. Especially in winter when it gets dark ridiculously early.

I'll sit by the lily pond and listen to the water hitting the stones, and for a minute it feels like the rest of the world forgot this place exists.

choices.choiceText: Even if everyone else forgets this place, I won't.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I'm holding onto that promise, {PlayerName}. More than you probably realize.

Let me show you what I'm keeping alive tonight before the night misting valve kicks in.

choices.choiceText: Show me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I've got my field sketchbook open on the cedar table under the little clip-on lamp. Watercolors, seed pods, root sketches... the whole messy pile.

I was working on this one earlier. Take a look:

choices.choiceText: Examine the highland pitcher plant watercolor plate.

nodes.partnerMessage:
See that rim around the pitcher? The tiny ridges and the wet surface make it ridiculously hard for insects to keep their footing, so they slide straight down into the trap.

It looks like little red porcelain. Then you remember the plant is basically baiting something to dinner.

choices.choiceText: That detail is gorgeous. You really captured the veining.
Carnivorous plants are such a weird mix of beautiful and ruthless.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you. I mixed the red from iron oxide and gum arabic until it looked right.

Honestly, painting a plant is one of the best ways to notice details I'd probably skip in a normal lab note. You can't fake a vein when you're staring at it for an hour.

choices.choiceText: You care about your science the way an artist cares about a painting. I like that about you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Botanical illustration used to be a normal part of science. Now everyone takes three phone photos and calls it a day.

I know it's slower, but... I like the slow way.

choices.choiceText: I like that. What else are you working on tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
It is ruthless, but I don't think it's cruel. Those bogs are so low in nutrients that the plants basically had to find another way to survive.

Sometimes adapting means doing something that looks a little harsh from the outside.

choices.choiceText: Did you ever have to make those kinds of changes in your own life?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. I lost a few friends who couldn't understand why I'd choose lab work over parties and weekends out.

Money's been tight too. I stayed here anyway.

It was lonely for a while, but I learned how to make a life out of very little.

choices.choiceText: I don't think you just survived. You became someone pretty remarkable.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I'm literally sitting here in a dirty apron getting emotional over a message.

That's embarrassing.

But... you have a really gentle way of seeing me. I don't know how else to put it.

choices.choiceText: You're worth seeing clearly. Let me be here with you a little longer.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Mostly checking the gauges, mixing a little seaweed tonic, and drinking peppermint tea while I look out at the foggy quad.

Not exactly a thrilling midnight operation. But honestly? I love it.

choices.choiceText: Honestly, that sounds nice. What are you working on?

nodes.partnerMessage:
If you came in here thinking I'd be easy to flirt with just because I spend half my life around ferns... you read me wrong.

I opened the private feed because I thought you actually wanted a quieter conversation.

Was I wrong?

choices.choiceText: You weren't wrong. I made a thoughtless comment, Masie. I'm sorry.
Relax, it was just a joke.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Thank you for just apologizing. No excuses, no trying to talk your way around it. I appreciate that.

Come on. I'll show you what I'm working on tonight.

choices.choiceText: I'm listening, Masie.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I've got twelve trays of highland *Nepenthes* hybrids that need repotting before the temperature drops this weekend.

The mix is mostly long-fiber sphagnum with perlite and a little pine bark. Nothing exciting until you see the roots.

Look at this chart. Week eight is where the primary root gets stupidly delicate.

choices.choiceText: That taproot looks like raw spun silk. If you pinch it with bare fingers, does it snap?
Why use New Zealand sphagnum instead of standard Canadian peat?
Are you sure the greenhouse boiler can hold the humidity if a frost hits tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
It snaps like wet thread. Seriously. One bad pinch and you've set the seedling back for weeks.

I have to tuck the moss around it with these tiny curved tweezers—

Wait.

*Distant metallic clank through the steam line.*

...What was that?

choices.choiceText: Masie? What made that sound?
Did the steam heating pipes just stutter?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Canadian peat gets dense and nasty pretty quickly here. The long-fiber sphagnum stays much airier, which these roots love.

Wait—

*Sharp thud from somewhere below.*

Oh no. That's the auxiliary boiler line.

choices.choiceText: Is something wrong with the heating system?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
The auxiliary boiler's been making that awful chattering sound all week. If the pressure drops too far tonight, the epiphyte wing could get cold fast.

Wait—

*Loud hiss. Metal rattling.*

The pressure gauge just dipped.

choices.choiceText: Masie?! Did the pilot flame blow out?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
The auxiliary boiler just tripped. The tropical wing is already down to 58°F and dropping.

I have to run into the cellar and open the bypass manually, and of course I picked tonight to have five trays of bare-root seedlings sitting out.

I'm calling you. Please pick up and stay with me for a minute, okay?

choices.choiceText: Incoming Call from Masie... [Accept Call]

nodes.partnerMessage: *Audio connecting... echoing footsteps, then the hiss of steam.*

*deep breath*

It's back. Bypass valve's seated, pilot's lit, and the pressure climbed over 22 PSI again. I can already feel the heat coming through the floor grates.

{PlayerName}... when my hands were slipping on that stupid brass valve and you kept talking me through it, I didn't spiral. You kept me calm.

I'm sitting on the bottom cellar step now with grease all over my hands.

choices.choiceText: You handled that like a pro. Your seedlings are safe.
Take a breath on that step. How are your hands holding up after that wrench work?
Hearing you wrench that brass valve open was intense! You have real strength in those arms.
Now that the temperature is climbing, come up out of the cellar.

nodes.partnerMessage:
They're safe. All twelve trays are under the heat lamps now, and the leaves are already starting to bead with moisture again.

If that pilot hadn't caught, months of work could've been gone by morning.

And... having you stay on the line really helped. My hands were shaking more than I wanted to admit.

choices.choiceText: Guess I'm your emergency hotline now.
Does anyone ever have your back when stuff like that happens?

nodes.partnerMessage:
...That's a really comforting thing to hear.

Usually when something breaks in here, it's just me, a flashlight, and whatever ancient piece of metal decided to fail.

Having your voice in my ear made it feel a lot less lonely.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to work in the dark alone anymore. Come sit by the pond.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Not really. The facilities crew is gone by five, and security mostly checks the outside.

When something goes wrong after hours, it's usually just me.

You're the only person who stayed awake and stuck around because you wanted to know I was okay.

choices.choiceText: Because you matter to me. More than these little messages.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay. That one got me.

I'm wiping soot off my hands right now, and I'm actually smiling. It's been a rough week, so... thank you.

choices.choiceText: Keep that smile. Now come upstairs and rest.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My thumb got a little scraped when the wrench slipped, but it's nothing dramatic.

I'm washing it at the cellar sink now. The hot water feels amazing after that cold metal.

choices.choiceText: Put some salve on that scrape. Then come back upstairs.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Try hauling bags of perlite all week and wrestling with old cast-iron valves.

Botanists are secretly strong, {PlayerName}. Don't let the quiet voice fool you. And definitely don't challenge me to arm wrestling.

choices.choiceText: Okay, okay. I yield. Now come upstairs.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Coming back up the stairs now. Closing the cellar door.

The palm house is warm again. The mist's settled into this soft haze under the ironwork, and everything smells like damp moss.

I'm heading over to the lily pond.

choices.choiceText: Go sit on the slate bench and decompress for a minute.
How's the lily pond looking tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
The *Victoria amazonica* pads are spread all over the dark water. Huge things. The pond is almost completely still.

I just sat down on the slate edge. The stone's warm from the boiler, so it feels like nature's version of a heated seat.

choices.choiceText: That sounds like the most peaceful place in the whole city.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Sitting down. Sweater pulled over my knees.

*deep exhale*

You know what's kind of funny? Before tonight, this greenhouse always felt like something I had to protect by myself.

Right now, with your messages on my screen... it just feels like home.

choices.choiceText: Because you don't have to defend it alone anymore. I'm here.
You built something really special here. It's obvious.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you... That word means more to me than you probably realize.

Everything feels disposable lately. I think that's why I care so much about fragile things. Keeping them alive feels like choosing not to let everything disappear.

choices.choiceText: You put so much care into this place. You deserve that same care back.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Home.

I haven't thought about my grandmother's kitchen in a while. That's what this word reminds me of.

Funny that a greenhouse at midnight is where I ended up feeling that kind of warmth again.

choices.choiceText: Because warmth comes from the person you're sharing the space with. Not the building.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My thermos is empty, my hands are warm again, and I'm just watching the iron rafters in the pond reflection.

{PlayerName}... when you picked up earlier and stayed with me while everything was going wrong, it felt like something in my shoulders finally unclenched.

Come by the conservatory gate Saturday afternoon.

I've got a terracotta pot, some fresh loam, and that cutting from my grandmother's Christmas cactus I told you about. I think you'd like it.

choices.choiceText: Saturday afternoon. I'll be there. Get some rest tonight.
I'll bring fresh bread from the bakery. So... I guess it's a date.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Saturday afternoon, then. I'll leave the south gate unlocked for you.

We'll make peppermint verbena tea, pot your cutting together, and sit by the glass while the sun warms the place back up.

Goodnight, {PlayerName}.

And... thanks for looking past all the soil and seeing me. Sleep well.

Status: Read just now.

Masie has closed the greenhouse communication log.

choices.choiceText: Masie? Did you lose signal down there?
I'm sorry, Masie. I was being cynical and dismissive of something you love. Please let me restart.
Leaving me on read in a greenhouse is kind of dramatic, you know.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Status: Read 25m ago.

[Typing...]

Masie has set her status to 'Offline - Tending Root Stock'.

The audio line cut out right when the steam valve started hissing. 

I'm still by the auxiliary pipe with the wrench. Call me back as soon as your signal settles, okay?

choices.choiceText: I'm back. Calling you now!

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think I'm going to lock up the glasshouse and leave the conversation here.

We clearly see this place—and some important things about life—very differently, and I don't have the energy for a cynical back-and-forth in the one place I come for peace.

Take care.

I spend most of my day taking care of fragile living things. I don't want to spend my private time arguing with someone who treats everything like a transaction.

You're removed from the greenhouse feed. Take care.

You know, I keep expecting you to ask me something clever about plants.

Instead you're just here. Which is... nice.

How was your day, though? Not the polished version. The actual one.

choices.choiceText: Honestly? A little messy. But talking to you is making it better.
I don't want to make tonight about me. Tell me what you need right now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's fair. Mine was messy too.

I think people imagine someone who works in a greenhouse spends all day calmly watering things in linen clothes.

Today I fought with a pump, broke a label, and got dirt in my phone speaker.

choices.choiceText: Okay, the dirt-in-your-phone part made me laugh.
And somehow you're still here taking care of everything.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Right now?

Honestly... company. Nothing dramatic. Just knowing there's somebody on the other side of the screen who doesn't need me to perform.

choices.choiceText: Then you have company. You don't need to perform for me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I knew that would be the part you laughed at.

I spent ten minutes trying to get the speaker dry with a tiny fan. Very scientific. Extremely dignified.

choices.choiceText: Extremely dignified. Five stars for fieldwork.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's kind of the job, I guess.

Something breaks, something wilts, something surprises you, and you deal with it. Then you come back the next day.

choices.choiceText: That sounds a lot like life, honestly.
And you don't have to come back tomorrow alone either.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay.

Then I'm taking you at your word.

No polished greenhouse-girl act tonight. I'm in an old sweater, my hair is a mess, and there is literally potting soil on my knee.

choices.choiceText: That sounds much more like the Masie I want to know.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. I think that's why I get attached to this place.

It reminds me that something can be damaged and still be worth tending to.

choices.choiceText: I like that. I think people can be like that too.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You keep saying things like that and then wondering why I get attached.

It's unfair, you know.

choices.choiceText: Attached already? That's kind of adorable.
Maybe I don't mind you getting attached.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Oh, so you're saying you like the messy version?

Careful. I might actually believe you.

choices.choiceText: I do. The messy version feels more real.
I might need photographic evidence before I commit to that statement.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Maybe that's the part I'm slowly learning.

You can't keep everything perfect. You can just decide what deserves your effort.

choices.choiceText: And I'm pretty happy I ended up being one of the things you gave some effort to.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Don't make me say it out loud. I have a reputation to maintain.

Also, you're making me smile at my phone like an idiot.

choices.choiceText: Good. I like being the reason.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...That's dangerous information to give me at midnight.

I get sentimental when I'm tired.

choices.choiceText: Then be sentimental. I'm not going anywhere tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Good.

Because the polished version of me gets tired too.

I'd rather you know the girl who forgets where she put her gloves and talks to seedlings when she's stressed.

choices.choiceText: Honestly, that girl sounds pretty easy to like.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Absolutely not. You'd weaponize it forever.

Besides, you'll see the mess in person someday.

choices.choiceText: Someday, huh? I'll remember you said that.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Please do.

Actually... Saturday is already sounding suspiciously like a very good excuse.

choices.choiceText: Then I'll see you Saturday, messy sweater and all.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You're making this private feed dangerously good for my ego.

I should probably go back to repotting something before I start getting all soft on you.

choices.choiceText: Too late. You're already soft on me.
Go on, botanist. I'll keep you company while you work.
